m8-defect1-newline.title: REWORK defect 1 -- newline guard tied to splitlines(), not a hand-listed char set
m8-defect1-newline.imperative: Reviewer BLOCK finding (touches C3b): _reject_newline() only checks literal \n/\r, but parse_episode() sections the file via str.splitlines(), which treats a WIDER set as line boundaries (\v, \f, \x1c-\x1e, \x85 NEL, U+2028, U+2029). A value embedding e.g. U+2028 passes the guard, writes once, then silently truncates on the next parse -- the exact injection class C3b exists to prevent. Fix: redefine the guard's predicate in terms of str.splitlines() itself (e.g. reject when value.splitlines() != [value], which catches both the multi-segment case AND the trailing-separator case like 'text\u2028' that splitlines() reduces to one element but is still unsafe) so the guard and the parser can never drift apart again. Add a code comment explaining WHY the predicate is defined via the parser's own behavior rather than an enumerated character list. Update _reject_newline's docstring to match. Add tests to tests/test_episode_store.py covering U+2028, U+2029, \v, \f, \x85 (NEL), and the trailing-separator case, plus at least one END-TO-END test that a forged '- status: retired' line via one of these characters is rejected (not just that the predicate returns True in isolation). TDD: write the new tests first, observe them fail against the old character-list guard, then fix.

preconditions.statement: g2 handoff and reviewer BLOCK (g2-review-result.md) reread; defect reproduced locally before fixing

postconditions.statement: TDD red: new newline-guard tests written and observed failing against the OLD character-list guard -- manual attest

m9-defect2-atomicity.title: REWORK defect 2 -- stage-then-commit write phase, so a mid-write I/O failure leaves the store untouched
m9-defect2-atomicity.imperative: Reviewer BLOCK finding (touches C4): _Transaction.commit() writes each touched file sequentially with no staging/rollback -- a failure on the 2nd of 2 writes (disk full, permission denied, locked file) leaves the 1st file's write landed while the delta as a whole fails, contradicting the module docstring's unconditional all-or-nothing claim. Fix: write every touched file to a temp path first (inside the store directory, so the later move is same-filesystem), and only once ALL staged writes succeed, move each into place via os.replace() (atomic for a single file on Windows and POSIX). On any staging failure, clean up the temp files already written and leave the store untouched. Add a code comment stating honestly that multi-file atomicity across the MOVE step is best-effort (a crash mid-move can still leave a partial result) -- do not overclaim full multi-file atomicity. Add a test that monkeypatches the write or move step to fail on the second of two touched files and asserts the store is byte-for-byte unchanged afterward (capture full directory state before, compare after). TDD: write the failing test against the OLD sequential-write code first, observe it fail, then fix.

postconditions.statement: TDD red: the forced-second-write-failure test written and observed failing against the OLD sequential commit() -- manual attest
stage-then-commit implemented; forced-failure test proves the store is untouched on a mid-write failure; full episode-store suite green

constraints: temp files must stay inside the store directory (same filesystem as the final move target)

m10-sweep.title: Sweep for the same defect class: an invariant enforced with one definition where a different part of the module assumes another
m10-sweep.imperative: Both BLOCK defects share one root cause: a validator's notion of well-formedness diverges from what the parser/renderer/a later reader actually assumes. Sweep scripts/apply_episode_delta.py end to end for other instances of this class -- e.g. ID_RE/RUN_RE vs how ids are actually constructed and parsed, FIELD_RE's assumptions vs what render_episode() emits, any other place a character set or format is validated by one rule but consumed by a different one. Fix anything found that is a live risk within scope; report anything judged safe (with reasoning) even if not fixed. No code change is required if the sweep finds nothing else load-bearing, but the imperative is not satisfied by skipping the sweep.

postconditions.statement: sweep performed across the whole module; findings (fixed or judged-safe) recorded for the result writeup -- manual attest
postconditions.satisfied_by: Swept every re.compile/strip()/write_text/read_text site in scripts/apply_episode_delta.py for the same class (a validator's well-formedness definition diverging from a parser/renderer/reader's own). Findings: (1) all free-text values rendered into a store line (mechanical scalars, artifact-ref entries, assertion statement/history, retire reason/retired-at/consolidated-into/superseded-by) route through _reject_newline before write -- confirmed by tracing every call site, no gap found. (2) ID_RE/RUN_RE (validate op-supplied ids) vs _next_episode_id's actual construction (run+'-'+3-digit seq): ID_RE is stricter-or-equal to what the writer ever constructs, and both further exclude any splitlines()-boundary char (RUN_RE's charset has none, and run is ALSO passed through _reject_newline in the mechanical-fields loop -- double-guarded, no gap). (3) FIELD_RE/ASSERTION_HEADING_RE/HEADER_RE (parse-side) vs render_episode()'s actual output format: traced field-by-field, every rendered '- key: value' line's value is guard-clean (single-line) by construction, so FIELD_RE's per-line assumption always holds; ASSERTION_HEADING_RE's id.aid tokens are writer-controlled (never free text). (4) checked str.strip()'s interaction with the guard: Python classifies several splitlines() boundary chars (\x1c-\x1e, \x85, U+2028/2029, \v treated similarly) as whitespace, so a value that is ONLY a boundary char gets caught earlier by _require_str's not-value.strip() empty check with a different but still-correct rejection message; a value with real content plus a boundary char reaches _reject_newline and is caught there -- verified both paths reject, no silent-accept gap either way. (5) noted, not fixed (pre-existing, unchanged by this rework, low risk): commit()'s per-write path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) runs before that file's write, so a staging failure on write N can leave an empty directory created for write N's parent (relevant only under the not-yet-ratified Option-A layout, which creates active/retired subdirs) -- an empty, untracked directory, not corrupted data; flagged as a cheap future tidy, not a live risk. No other instances of the class found; no additional code changes made beyond the two already-fixed defects.
